problem: Existing surveys review semantic mapping only inside downstream task advances (navigation, manipulation, SLAM), so there is no unified view of how semantic maps are built and represented independently of the task. Map quality itself is rarely evaluated.
motivation: Foundation models are driving demand for general-purpose, open-vocabulary, queryable, task-agnostic map representations. The design choices behind such maps (structure, encoding, evaluation) need a principled comparison to guide future work.
key_idea: Organize the semantic map-building literature along two axes, map structure (spatial grid, topological, dense geometric, hybrid) and semantic encoding (explicit vs implicit V/VL features), and use that taxonomy to analyze trade-offs, evaluation gaps, challenges and future directions.
insight: The field is moving from closed-vocabulary explicit maps toward open-vocabulary implicit VL maps (value maps, VLMaps, ConceptGraphs) that can be built once and reused across tasks. The main open costs are memory and compute. The survey also finds that intrinsic map evaluation (accuracy, completeness, consistency, robustness) is almost entirely missing, so it is unclear whether task gains come from better maps or better policies. Hybrid and dense geometric maps are under-explored in embodied AI. This is a qualitative survey with no ablations.
method: Taxonomy: two axes, structure (grid, topological, dense geometric incl. point clouds/surfels/NeRF/Gaussian splats, hybrid) and encoding (explicit occupancy/explored/category/visit time; implicit visual or visual-language; implicit-to-explicit).
Background: covers embodied and robotics tasks, SLAM and Semantic SLAM basics, and end-to-end vs modular pipelines (visual encoder, mapper, exploration, planner).

Map building pipeline: localization, feature extraction, projection (pinhole to orthographic grid), and accumulation (overwrite, max, mean, GRU); also egocentric vs allocentric frames, online vs offline building.
Per-structure and per-encoding review: comparison tables for spatial grid maps, topological maps, dense geometric maps and open-vocabulary maps (encoder, training, planner, aggregation).
Evaluation review: extrinsic metrics (SR, SPL, NE, nDTW, etc.) vs proposed intrinsic dimensions (accuracy, completeness, consistency, robustness).

Challenges and future directions: efficiency, scalability, real-time processing, noise and uncertainty, multi-modal fusion, lifelong learning, standardized evaluation; general-purpose, dense-yet-efficient, dynamic and hybrid maps.
numbers_note: Survey paper; no experimental results reported.
results: No experiments. The survey reports that the field is converging on open-vocabulary, queryable, task-agnostic maps, while high memory demand and computational inefficiency remain open. It also identifies missing intrinsic map evaluation and under-explored hybrid and dense maps.
limitations: Focused on indoor, room-scale navigation, with only brief coverage of outdoor, driving and manipulation mapping.
Qualitative taxonomy with no quantitative cross-method comparison.
Coverage is limited to the papers the authors selected and can go out of date given the rapid pace of foundation-model mapping work.
compares_to: Song et al. 2025 (semantic mapping in indoor robotics survey)
Existing embodied AI surveys (Duan et al. 2022, Deitke et al. 2022)
